invariants: Identity, membership, tenant, row scope and entitlement are verified at request and job execution. A tenant ID supplied by a browser is never authorization.
Business FKs contain tenant_id; PostgreSQL runtime roles cannot bypass RLS or own tables. Every pooled transaction sets local verified context; missing context denies access.
Idempotency keys bind actor, tenant, operation and canonical input hash. Domain changes and outbox events commit in the same PostgreSQL transaction.
Content, forms, campaigns, metrics, routing policies, provider mappings, prompts and display policies are versioned. Conflicting edits never silently overwrite.
Sending checks current consent, suppression, resource state, scope, entitlements, quiet hours and provider readiness at dispatch. Unknown provider acceptance requires reconciliation.
Unknown permissions mean deny. Data display, media storage, caches, alerts, retention and AI use are independently gated by approved provider rights.
Until authorized connectivity, the only MLS source is the mock adapter and conspicuously fictional fixtures. Production live adapters reject synthetic data.
AI proposes drafts; acceptance saves a reviewed draft only. Publishing, sending, billing and consent changes remain explicit authorized commands.
A queued operation is not a completed operation. Unknown, zero, unavailable and stale metrics are different states with timestamps and definitions.
Module service ports and versioned events are the integration boundaries. Consumer modules do not directly mutate another module’s tables.
Revoked membership, staff grants, visitor sessions, feeds or consents invalidate future requests, jobs and signed downloads.
Audit observation, inferred technology and proposed architecture remain labeled. Runtime, licensing and commercial assumptions need their milestone gates.
adrs: NestJS modules expose service ports over one transactional database; Next.js and workers are independently deployable. This keeps tenant commands atomic and reduces operational overhead. Extract a service only after measured scaling or isolation needs justify it.

OpenAPI 3.1.1 and JSON Schema are shared contracts. Generate TypeScript clients and validate inputs at the boundary. No initial GraphQL layer: current list/detail/command flows fit REST and avoid a second authorization surface.

Use tenant-scoped relational filters, text indexes and geographic indexes. An external search engine is optional after measured query/index limits; rights expiry and authoritative policy still govern cached index results.

Use independently designed blocks, templates and a Puck editor adapter. Store data owned by the platform and render through Next.js. WordPress migration is a later adapter, not a requirement to operate two publishing systems.
Durability in PostgreSQL, wakeups in Redis

Persist jobs, scheduled actions and outbox rows in PostgreSQL. BullMQ manages concurrency and wakeups. A Redis loss must be recoverable by scanning due committed work; a Redis acknowledgment is not the business transaction.

One schema with composite tenant keys and FORCE RLS, plus application permission/row-scope guards. Separate databases per tenant remain an exceptional later deployment option; neither schema count nor a browser selector supplies security.
Support authorized replication, live-query and embed modes. Unsupported actions are hidden or explained; embed-only rights do not authorize native storage, alerts or AI retrieval.
OIDC Authorization Code + PKCE through a BFF; proposed Entra External ID. Stripe hosted payment/customer flows and verified webhooks. Local roles/entitlements stay platform-owned.

Use the OpenAI Responses API with strict schemas, scoped facts, evaluation gates and draft review. Pin model/prompt versions per release after measurement; do not make the architecture depend on a permanently named model.

Propose Azure Container Apps, managed PostgreSQL, private Redis, Blob Storage, Key Vault and CDN. OCI images and provider interfaces keep the application portable; provider procurement, region and capacity remain owner decisions.

modules.name: SaaS administration, identity and billing
modules.purpose: One organization, identity and entitlement model for agents, offices and product assets. Staff administration uses a separate control-plane context.

requirements.text: Provision an organization through a durable job: seed built-in roles, six configurable pipeline stages, default lead source and business profile; expose pending/ready/failed state. Invitations use a hashed, expiring, one-use token and require the signed-in verified email to match the invitation.

Support owner, organization manager, agent, marketing editor, billing administrator and read-only analyst role presets. Permission codes come from the API catalog; scope is own/team/organization. Custom roles cannot grant rights the caller cannot delegate. Lock the organization row during owner changes and reject removal or demotion of its final active owner.

Offer organization, office, member and business-profile management with optimistic versions, audit events and visible entitlement limits. An identity may belong to multiple organizations; the active organization selector changes all data, cache and job contexts together.

Show account subscription, enabled/pending/disabled capabilities, invoices, annual invoice total and monthly equivalent separately. Preview plan changes, cancellation/resumption, proration, currency, taxes and effective date; require an unexpired preview and explicit acceptance before a financial operation.

Stripe webhook reconciliation determines billing state; application entitlements remain explicit records. Duplicate or out-of-order events trigger a current provider-state read, not timestamp-only entitlement changes. Failed provisioning never becomes ready merely because payment succeeded.

Super administrators see organization health, provisioning jobs, feature configuration, subscription reconciliation, redacted audit logs and operational summaries. Access to customer records requires a time-bound, reasoned grant and visible staff-session banner; it is not an ordinary tenant role.

modules.name: CRM, leads, deals, tasks and routing
modules.purpose: Own the commercial relationship model independently of IDX or a white-label CRM provider.

requirements.text: Separate contact identity/channels from a lead opportunity and a deal. Maintain normalized email/phone values, source attribution, optional user-provided intent/timeline, tags, stage history, notes and a communication/activity timeline. Unknown values remain unknown.

Provide saved list filters, server pagination, column preferences, bulk selection scope, lead detail drawers and a pipeline view. Default stages are Uncontacted, Attempted Contact, Nurturing, Dead, Under Contract and Closed; organizations can configure their own immutable stage IDs.

Routing precedence defaults to first-touch owner, listing-attributed agent, geography, then weighted round robin. Evaluate only active eligible members; serialize distribution state, record the winning rule and fall back to an unassigned queue when no recipient is eligible. Office and tenant boundaries apply to every rule.

Score documented engagement signals using a versioned deterministic formula before introducing AI. Show reason codes and last event time; score is sales follow-up prioritization, never housing eligibility, protected-attribute inference or mortgage approval.

CSV imports require a scoped signed upload, mapping, preview, row errors, duplicate candidates and an explicit reviewed merge/skip policy. Commit the accepted snapshot with an idempotency key; do not merge automatically across organizations or solely because a household shares a phone.

Exports run as jobs with source-scope authorization at request and download, short-lived artifact access, spreadsheet-formula neutralization and audit. Archiving a contact/lead cancels eligible pending sends and marks public organizer relationships according to the retention plan.

Tasks require assignee, title, due instant and IANA timezone. Stage, owner and note changes use If-Match or expected version, preserve historical events and return conflict instead of silently overwriting another agent.

Ship independently designed agent, brokerage and landing template families. Template definitions are versioned repository assets; tenant customizations become content revisions.

Allow page, blog, landing, community, agent and testimonial documents with navigation, slug, SEO title/description, canonical path, social image and noindex settings. Offer hero, text, image, CTA, agent, testimonials, community, listing grid, search, form, map and footer blocks.

Save drafts as immutable revisions with optimistic document versions. Publish validates every block, image right, link, form and MLS capability, then atomically updates the revision pointer and emits cache invalidation. Preview and production have distinct hostnames and signed preview access; rollback republishes an existing compatible revision.

Unknown/older blocks preserve their data and render a safe editor warning; they cannot be silently dropped or published until migrated. Arbitrary scripts, SQL, unsafe HTML, remote fetch URLs and free-form executable custom CSS are excluded from the initial block contract.

Custom domains require ownership verification, a globally unique normalized hostname, TLS provisioning and exact host→site→organization mapping. A verification job never grants a hostname based on an unverified client claim. Detach revokes routing and certificates before the domain can be reassigned.

Media uploads are signed, tenant-prefixed, capped and MIME-sniffed, scanned before publication, transformed into responsive derivatives and attached to a rights attestation. Originals remain private unless explicitly permitted; SVG uploads are rejected or sanitized by a vetted pipeline, not embedded as executable user HTML.

Versioned form schemas define labels, required fields, bounds, select choices, honeypot/challenge, purpose-specific consent and confirmation. Server validation uses the published version. A durable transaction stores the entry, lead decision and outbox event before acknowledging. Ordinary form entry permits paste and accessible validation.

Initial forms do not offer public file uploads or pricing/payment fields. The API upload grant is staff-authenticated; public visitor file uploads require a later quota, scanning and abuse review. These are deferred from the reference Gravity Forms library rather than accidentally promised.

Public rendering is server-produced and SEO-friendly. Property blocks use approved public listing projections; a provider supporting only embeds cannot be presented as native searchable feed data. Hidden/deleted/expired listings invalidate page, map, image and alert caches.

acceptance: An editor can save a draft without publishing. Two editors changing the same document receive a conflict rather than losing content; rollback reproduces the selected published revision.
A malicious block/link/media URL or executable HTML is rejected; unsupported blocks remain recoverable. The public page cannot access another tenant’s media or draft revision.
Two organizations cannot claim the same hostname, including case/IDN-normalized variants. A spoofed Host header or unverified domain cannot select customer data.

A form retry records one lead decision and one consent evidence set. An unrecognized field, invalid published version, malicious size or unavailable commit returns a defined error without false success.
Published pages include correct canonical/robots/Open Graph and permitted listing attribution, with tested 360/768/1440px layout and keyboard block editing.

modules.name: Marketing, campaigns, consent and automation
modules.purpose: Own marketing policy and durable execution; use transport providers and a mature email editor without delegating the CRM source of truth.

requirements.text: Support reusable email/SMS designs, broadcast segment previews, send-later, drip campaigns, birthday/transaction-anniversary greetings and enrollment tables. Email design uses Unlayer when licensed; design JSON and rendered HTML are versioned together through EmailEditorAdapter.

Workflow nodes are wait/email/SMS/condition/task; graphs contain at most 100 nodes, one entry and no cycles. Conditions use an allowlisted lead-filter/event DSL, not arbitrary code. Preview runs on a deterministic virtual clock and identifies required channel/entitlement prerequisites.

Triggers include captured lead, property inquiry, saved search, favorite, stage change and anniversary. Enrollment policies are once, after completion, or after configured inactivity. Published versions are immutable; edits affect future enrollments unless an explicit migration/cancellation is approved.

Store scheduled actions durably in PostgreSQL. BullMQ/Redis dispatches wake-ups, not the only copy of a schedule. Workers acquire bounded leases, validate tenant scope, version, entitlement, contact archive state, consent, suppression, sender verification and quiet hours immediately before provider submission.

Email uses a proposed Resend adapter; SMS uses a proposed Twilio adapter with registration/opt-in gates. Development uses a no-delivery transport. Sender domain/number readiness is a real state, not inferred from a campaign active flag. Vendor callbacks determine submitted/delivered/bounced/failed; opens are explicitly non-guaranteed engagement signals.

Idempotency covers native actions and provider request keys, but provider guarantees are capability-specific and time-limited. A timed-out send with uncertain acceptance becomes unknown; reconcile with the provider before resubmission. Never promise universal exactly-once delivery.

Opt-outs produce a suppression/withdrawal event before further marketing work is eligible. Cancelled enrollments invalidate pending generation keys; already accepted provider sends may be unretractable and must be shown accurately. Replies and STOP-like events follow the approved provider/consent policy.

Quiet hours use the recipient’s known IANA timezone or an organization fallback with visible policy. For calendar schedules, choose the first valid instant after a spring gap and the earlier occurrence in a fall overlap; record the choice and execute once. Anniversary schedules define leap-day behavior explicitly.

acceptance: A worker crash, duplicate event or Redis loss does not lose the PostgreSQL schedule. Recovery does not create duplicate native action keys.

Unknown provider acceptance cannot enter the normal blind-retry path. Duplicate/out-of-order receipts do not regress delivered to submitted.

modules.name: Property search, organizer and Las Vegas MLS
modules.milestone: M1 contract; M5 mock; M6 live gate
modules.purpose: A provider-neutral property experience with feed rights, capability and freshness policies present from the first data model.

requirements.text: Implement the MlsAdapter contract with a mock provider first. Each feed declares replication, live query, embedding, incremental/deletion and media-caching capabilities. Native ingestion is used only where authorized; proxy-only and embed-only providers have explicit feature limits.

Normalize provider/board/source listing keys, source status, price/currency, address, coordinates, property type, bedrooms/baths, area units, public remarks, media, attribution, modification time and display restrictions. Preserve source fields needed for mapping internally; never expose raw agent/private fields.

Provide list/map search, location/bounding-box filters, price/type/bed/bath filters, safe keywords, pagination, stable sorting, details and a property inquiry. Map and list use the same filtered result definition; hidden addresses also hide exact coordinates according to the approved policy.

Saved properties/searches are owned by a site-bound verified visitor. Listing changes generate deduplicated alert matches; before notification, recheck feed permission, listing availability, alert preference and consent. Inquiry capture routes through the native CRM with source and listing provenance.

Incremental synchronization follows opaque provider paging/cursors, handles identical timestamps and overlap, upserts idempotently and advances a checkpoint only after durable processing. Deleted/withdrawn data disappears promptly through listing state, caches, search indexes and scheduled alerts. Missing deletion support requires contract-approved reconciliation.

DisplayPolicy governs field/status visibility, attribution, refresh/freshness, retention, cache, images and AI use. Unknown contract rights default to disabled; independent regional adapters do not share tenant/feed data without explicit licensed authorization.

The project owner selected CoreLogic Trestle (now Cotality Trestle) as the provider on 10 October 2026. Target its documented RESO WebAPI adapter; approved Las Vegas connection details and credentials arrive at M6. Confirm the actual board, feed product, participant permissions, endpoint, accessible metadata and display/retention/media rights then; public documentation does not establish account authorization.

Every mock record/page/map result and exported sample is marked SYNTHETIC DEMO DATA. The production live-feed configuration rejects mock connections and synthetic records; mock listing changes can only drive no-delivery transport in development/staging.

Expired, disallowed or stale-beyond-policy records do not appear in list, map, details, images or outbound alerts. Hidden address fields are not leaked through SEO/JSON-LD or coordinates.

modules.name: Reporting, attribution and product analytics
modules.purpose: Make platform outcomes auditable and comparable with published definitions rather than blended undocumented scorecards.

requirements.text: Define website session/page engagement, captured/qualified leads, contact rate, stage conversion, campaign submitted/delivered/bounced/clicked activity, pipeline value and listing engagement. Separate counts, unique entities, cohorts and estimates.

Metric definitions are versioned JSON contracts with event source, numerator, denominator, exclusion rules, deduplication, timezone and freshness. Initial aggregates live in PostgreSQL; introduce a warehouse/search service only after measured query/retention limits.

Campaign conversion joins eligible events to a documented attribution window and reports unattributed records. Email opens may be affected by privacy proxies; never equate opens with confirmed human reading or business conversion.

Reporting filters and exports respect underlying agent/team/organization permissions. Raw form/chat payloads and full contact records do not enter anonymous traffic telemetry. Respect approved analytics consent and collection configuration.

Display data source, last refresh and unavailable status. Provider metrics retain their original source/window; publisher coverage is reported separately from actual search visibility or AI assistant answers.

Provide period comparisons, funnel and pipeline views, campaign/listing drill-down and account operational health. Initial reports are bounded synchronous queries; heavy exports become scoped durable jobs.

Report row data and totals cannot exceed a caller’s CRM scope. Day boundaries and comparisons match the selected IANA timezone.
Unknown/missing provider statistics display unavailable and cannot be averaged into a synthetic success score.

modules.name: Assistive AI and competitive intelligence
modules.purpose: Assist people with drafting and understanding verified facts; AI is never a substitute for permission, licensed data rights or publication approval.

requirements.text: Provide optional page/blog drafts, property descriptions, campaign drafts, lead activity summaries, workflow suggestions and analytics explanations. Each job records purpose, requester, context references, prompt/model configuration version, usage, warnings and expiry.

Use a server-side OpenAI Responses API adapter with schema-constrained outputs and a configured model selected through evaluation. Do not hard-code a marketing model name as a permanent default. Handle refusal, incomplete output, timeout and schema-invalid results without applying a partial result.

Retrieve only tenant-scoped, permission-filtered facts, with an explicit MLS AI-use flag where listing data is involved. Distinguish source facts from generated prose; citations point to verified fields/documents and cannot be fabricated by accepting model-provided IDs blindly.

Acceptance of a draft checks the destination write permission and expected revision, then saves a draft/version through the domain service. It never publishes, sends a campaign, changes consent, modifies a billing plan or acts on a lead merely because an AI job succeeded.

Lead qualification assistance summarizes voluntarily supplied intent/timeline and interaction history. It must not infer protected characteristics, decide access to housing/credit, or score financial eligibility. Humans review follow-up recommendations.

A conversational public-site assistant is a separate later opt-in capability: public published content and permitted listings only, no CRM/customer retrieval. Begin with read-only FAQ/property answers, citations and handoff; property inquiries use the standard consent-aware form, not a hidden AI side effect.

Analytics explanations include actual metric definitions and computed values; the model does not calculate financial/KPI truth from prose. A provider-neutral guard prevents arbitrary URL fetching, unapproved tool use and cross-tenant retrieval induced by listing or user prompt injection.

Require per-organization cost/request caps, bounded context/output, redacted telemetry, configurable retention and an approved provider data agreement. store:false reduces response persistence where supported but is not a promise of zero provider retention.

A cancelled/refused/incomplete job leaves source records unchanged. Accepting a result fails if the destination version or permission changed.
Evaluation sets cover factuality, protected-attribute/eligibility requests, PII disclosure, prompt injection, useful abstention, schema compliance, cost and latency.

requirements.text: Maintain a canonical business profile for identity, contact, hours, categories, media and social links. A Yext adapter is the proposed first network provider; integration rights and API scope require procurement verification.

Report publisher sync coverage, reviews/reputation and source-specific visibility metrics with definitions. Any real query-based AI visibility tracking is a separate explicit measurement feature, not renamed directory coverage.

Google Business connection, social scheduling and review-response workflows remain capability/permission gated. AI-assisted review responses are drafts that require human approval and a provider-supported publication method.

Reusable brand kits and email/page templates are launch features. Standalone print fulfillment, design packs, mortgage-specific products and advanced creative editors are deferred until product demand, licensing and fulfillment behavior are verified.

modules.name: Support, integration operations and account health
modules.purpose: Make provisioning and provider problems visible, recoverable and supportable without invisible staff access.

requirements.text: Create/read scoped support tickets with subject, category and detailed description; maintain a ticket-event timeline with actor and status. Attachments are deferred until the upload/retention pipeline supports them.

Expose customer-safe integration status and jobs: queued/running/succeeded/failed/unknown, attempts, last success, safe error code and recommended action. Never display secrets, provider raw payloads or another organization’s support record.

Provide staff dashboards for failed provisioning, billing/feed reconciliation, sender eligibility, expired domains and worker lag. Replay is an explicit audited domain action with idempotency and scope validation, not a generic rerun-any-payload button.
Document onboarding and contextual help. Replace reference achievement/help clutter with task-relevant learning; do not assume a tutorial link means the named service is integrated.

modules.name: Full web application and installable iPhone/Android experience
modules.milestone: M1 foundation; M2–M7 workflow parity; M8 device gate
modules.purpose: Deliver the same complete web application through browsers and home-screen installation on iPhone and Android, without App Store or Google Play distribution.

requirements.text: Implement an HTTPS Progressive Web App using Next.js manifest support, an original icon set, display:standalone, stable manifest id, start URL, app scope and service worker. The workspace remains usable in ordinary browsers without installation. No native wrapper or app-store submission is part of the architecture.

Provide platform-appropriate installation guidance: iPhone browser share/menu Add to Home Screen and Android Install/Add to Home Screen. Detect install capability and standalone mode; never show a nonfunctional universal install button or block use behind installation.

Make every entitled workflow usable at 360px and larger: CRM capture/edit/tasks, dashboards, builder draft/preview/publish, campaign edit/preview/confirm, property search/inquiry/organizer, reports, settings and authorized administration. Complex canvases have accessible list/form alternatives; do not require a desktop to complete core commands.

Respect device safe areas, dynamic viewport height, orientation, virtual keyboards, touch targets, screen readers and system text enlargement. Preserve deep links and navigation history; reauthenticate safely after suspension, external OIDC and hosted billing flows.

Cache only approved static application assets and a generic offline screen. Initial release is online-first: no private CRM, session tokens, personalized HTML/RSC, messages, exports, AI results or MLS data in service-worker caches or IndexedDB. Offline mutations are visibly disabled and never reported as saved.

Preserve unsaved changes in current tab memory during brief connection loss and warn before navigation/update; process eviction may discard them. After reconnection refetch versions and permissions. Durable offline editing/synchronization is deferred to a separately reviewed data-conflict/security design.

Use versioned static asset caches and a waiting-worker update notice. Never force reload while a draft is dirty or a payment/publish/send confirmation is in flight. Reload only after user acceptance or a safe idle transition, and remove obsolete non-sensitive caches.

Offer opt-in standards-based Web Push for assigned-lead, task-due and job-failure notices where supported; the in-app inbox remains authoritative. Check capabilities and user gesture, handle denied permission, and keep lock-screen text generic with no contact/property details.

Store encrypted, tenant/member-scoped push subscriptions and revoke devices on explicit removal/logout and membership revocation. Validate HTTPS push endpoints against approved provider egress policy; reject local/private hosts. VAPID private keys are server secrets; push clicks open allowlisted same-origin deep links and recheck authorization.

M8 requires physical iPhone Safari/browser and installed-home-screen tests, plus Android Chrome/browser and installed tests. Cover sign-in, organization switching, all core workflows, interruptions/offline, SW upgrades, denied push, device removal, keyboard/safe-area behavior and no sensitive persistent caching.

A waiting service-worker update does not discard dirty editor content or duplicate a submitted command. Browser-tab use works when installation or push is unavailable.

sections.title: 1. Delivery, scope and decision status
sections.html:
This is a development blueprint, not an implemented application. All new behavior, schemas, APIs, fixtures, diagrams and performance targets are proposed. The SQL has not been executed against PostgreSQL; provider contracts, costs and production readiness remain milestone gates.

Build an independent platform around one verified organization context, a native CRM, versioned websites and marketing, and a property layer that honors the eventual Las Vegas provider’s capabilities. Prioritize complete daily workflows and dependable outcomes over recreating every reference product.

Design baselineScope
Version / dateTDD 1.0 · 10 October 2026 · Asia/Bangkok
Evidence inputEntire prior audit, structured source · Original audit and retained evidence bundle
Core launchM1–M5 foundation, SaaS/CRM, CMS, marketing, full mobile/PWA workflows and clearly synthetic IDX; live Las Vegas IDX needs M6 approval.
Competitive enhancementsM7 assistive AI, defined reporting and optional local visibility; advanced design/print studio, rank tracking and mortgage calculators deferred.
Practical artifacts72 table definitions; 170 API operations; 11 modules; 12 workstreams; 8 milestone gates; 72 audit-feature mappings.
TerminologyOrganization = tenant; member = identity’s organization membership; visitor = site-bound public organizer identity; platform staff = separate control plane.
Independent designOriginal navigation, tokens, content models and code. No copied Agent Elite source, proprietary templates or restricted MLS records.

Commercial decisions still open: brand, exact plans/limits, hosting region, traffic forecast, provider procurement, retention obligations and launch scope. Proposed defaults make implementation concrete; owners approve these at the relevant gate. Do not delay M1 on live MLS credentials or presume that every listed connector is required.

Non-negotiable implementation invariants

IDBoundaryRequired behavior
INV-01Verified contextIdentity, membership, tenant, row scope and entitlement are verified at request and job execution. A tenant ID supplied by a browser is never authorization.
INV-02Database boundaryBusiness FKs contain tenant_id; PostgreSQL runtime roles cannot bypass RLS or own tables. Every pooled transaction sets local verified context; missing context denies access.
INV-03One durable commandIdempotency keys bind actor, tenant, operation and canonical input hash. Domain changes and outbox events commit in the same PostgreSQL transaction.
INV-04Explicit versionsContent, forms, campaigns, metrics, routing policies, provider mappings, prompts and display policies are versioned. Conflicting edits never silently overwrite.
INV-05Delivery eligibilitySending checks current consent, suppression, resource state, scope, entitlements, quiet hours and provider readiness at dispatch. Unknown provider acceptance requires reconciliation.
INV-06MLS rights before visibilityUnknown permissions mean deny. Data display, media storage, caches, alerts, retention and AI use are independently gated by approved provider rights.
INV-07Synthetic developmentUntil authorized connectivity, the only MLS source is the mock adapter and conspicuously fictional fixtures. Production live adapters reject synthetic data.
INV-08Human AI controlAI proposes drafts; acceptance saves a reviewed draft only. Publishing, sending, billing and consent changes remain explicit authorized commands.
INV-09Truthful outcomesA queued operation is not a completed operation. Unknown, zero, unavailable and stale metrics are different states with timestamps and definitions.
INV-10No hidden cross-module writesModule service ports and versioned events are the integration boundaries. Consumer modules do not directly mutate another module’s tables.
INV-11Revocation applies everywhereRevoked membership, staff grants, visitor sessions, feeds or consents invalidate future requests, jobs and signed downloads.
INV-12Evidence and proposed behaviorAudit observation, inferred technology and proposed architecture remain labeled. Runtime, licensing and commercial assumptions need their milestone gates.

sections.title: 2. Audit translation and feature comparison
sections.html:
The source audit reviewed authenticated portal, white-label CRM/IDX, WordPress and public website surfaces. It retained 72 feature observations, 30 technology findings, 28 integration entries, 15 workflows and 14 gaps. UI or source evidence demonstrates a surface; it does not prove writes, business enforcement, message delivery, feed licensing or production latency. No audit finding establishes the actual database engine.

Reference layerEvidence labelArchitecture implication
PortalConfirmed: Bootstrap/jQuery assets, Kestrel response marker and Azure AD B2C flow. Inferred: .NET/Razor-family rendering; backend internals unknown.Replace product launches and duplicate identity boundaries with one native workspace.
CRM / IDXConfirmed: iHomefinder/IDXHome surfaces, React 17 bundle and cross-origin control-panel API. Bundled libraries do not establish every active integration.Native tenant-scoped CRM; replace remote account handoff. Property data access remains provider-dependent.
Website editingConfirmed: WordPress 6.8.5, Genesis-family Monterey/Awesomeberg, Gutenberg, Gravity Forms and Yoast assets. Origin hosting/database unproven.Independent blocks/templates, stable revision model, clearer errors and one publishing workflow.
Communication / billingConfirmed: Unlayer designer and Stripe handoff/receipt surface. Actual email/SMS transport and exact payment implementation unknown.License an editor if justified; own orchestration and use separately verified delivery/payment adapters.
Local visibility / Design StudioYext-backed portal API observed. Advanced destination inspection blocked; premium design editor features documented only.Do not invent advanced runtime behavior. Defer unclear products; distinguish coverage proxies from measured AI-answer visibility.
UX / performanceAudit found ambiguous metric denominators, pricing presentation, editor warnings and a small blue CTA contrast ratio 2.753:1. Uncompressed bundle size was observed, not a latency benchmark.Defined metrics and costs, accessible shared components, lazy editors/maps and measured budgets.

“Match” preserves useful behavior. “Improve” strengthens a verified surface. “Redesign” changes the model or workflow. “Defer” keeps an option outside launch. “Remove” excludes a proposed equivalent of an unsubstantiated metric. Each row preserves its inspection limitation; a documented or gated feature is not promoted to verified runtime behavior.

URL owns filter state; local React owns transient UI. No initial Redux store. React Hook Form with shared JSON Schema/Ajv validation. Tailwind theme variables

Database / migrationsManaged PostgreSQL 17 + PostGIS; Drizzle + node-postgresSQL is explicit and reviewed; ORM does not replace RLS. Compatible supported versions are pinned after M1 migration tests. Do not call the provided baseline a validated migration. Drizzle query documentation
Jobs / cacheBullMQ + Redis, PostgreSQL outbox/jobsBounded concurrency, persistent Redis with noeviction and private TLS; Redis wakes durable database work. Tenant-local idempotency and job leases survive queue redelivery. BullMQ production guidance
CMS / email editorPuck adapter; versioned native blocks; Unlayer adapterPuck keeps the platform’s content data and rendering. Email editor licensing and export support need procurement; editable email JSON and sanitized rendered output are stored together. Puck documentation Unlayer email builder
Authentication / billingEntra External ID OIDC; StripeUse a new customer identity service rather than assume access to a legacy B2C purchase. Hosted identity does not supply organization authorization. Merchant configuration and taxes require M2 setup. External ID customer overview
CommunicationResend email; Twilio SMS; provider portsProposed providers, not audited Agent Elite transport claims. Sandbox/no-delivery before launch; verify domain, SMS readiness, receipts, signatures and quota capabilities. Resend API Twilio webhook requests
Maps / searchPostGIS + PostgreSQL text; MapLibre + licensed tiles/geocodingUse a MapTiler or equivalent adapter after procurement. No production dependence on demo/public tiles. List views remain available without maps; bound bbox and query cost. PostGIS distance query
AI / observabilityOpenAI Responses API; OpenTelemetry; managed metrics/logsModel and prompt choices follow evaluations. Correlation and safe error codes, no raw message bodies or credentials in telemetry. Provider outage degrades draft assistance without blocking CRM. OpenAI structured outputs
InfrastructureAzure Container Apps; PostgreSQL; Blob; Key Vault; CDN; TerraformSeparate web/API/worker scaling and migration job. Private database/cache, managed identities, independently scoped storage and secret references. Optional Sentry requires approved redaction/region; no Kubernetes initially.

Deploy one web image, one API image and one worker image from the same revision. The workspace and public renderer may be split into separate deployments later if cache policy or load requires it; they share block and contract packages now. API commands perform authorization and domain validation before a short database transaction. Provider calls use timeouts and bounded retries outside that transaction. Publishing and delivery complete through durable jobs.

Keep domain modules internally layered: controller → validated command/query → policy → service → repository. Service ports return domain DTOs, never raw ORM models. Jobs contain identifiers and expected versions rather than serialized customer records or tokens. Never make a public SSR handler depend on a tenant-wide CRM query.

Architectural decisions

ADRDecisionRationale
ADR-001Modular monolith with separate workersNestJS modules expose service ports over one transactional database; Next.js and workers are independently deployable. This keeps tenant commands atomic and reduces operational overhead. Extract a service only after measured scaling or isolation needs justify it.
ADR-002Contracts first, REST firstOpenAPI 3.1.1 and JSON Schema are shared contracts. Generate TypeScript clients and validate inputs at the boundary. No initial GraphQL layer: current list/detail/command flows fit REST and avoid a second authorization surface.
ADR-003PostgreSQL/PostGIS search firstUse tenant-scoped relational filters, text indexes and geographic indexes. An external search engine is optional after measured query/index limits; rights expiry and authoritative policy still govern cached index results.
ADR-004Native website content modelUse independently designed blocks, templates and a Puck editor adapter. Store data owned by the platform and render through Next.js. WordPress migration is a later adapter, not a requirement to operate two publishing systems.
ADR-005Durability in PostgreSQL, wakeups in RedisPersist jobs, scheduled actions and outbox rows in PostgreSQL. BullMQ manages concurrency and wakeups. A Redis loss must be recoverable by scanning due committed work; a Redis acknowledgment is not the business transaction.
ADR-006Tenant isolation in depthOne schema with composite tenant keys and FORCE RLS, plus application permission/row-scope guards. Separate databases per tenant remain an exceptional later deployment option; neither schema count nor a browser selector supplies security.
ADR-007Provider capabilities determine IDX UXSupport authorized replication, live-query and embed modes. Unsupported actions are hidden or explained; embed-only rights do not authorize native storage, alerts or AI retrieval.
ADR-008Hosted identity and paymentsOIDC Authorization Code + PKCE through a BFF; proposed Entra External ID. Stripe hosted payment/customer flows and verified webhooks. Local roles/entitlements stay platform-owned.
ADR-009Assistive AI behind an adapterUse the OpenAI Responses API with strict schemas, scoped facts, evaluation gates and draft review. Pin model/prompt versions per release after measurement; do not make the architecture depend on a permanently named model.
ADR-010Managed infrastructure, portable applicationsPropose Azure Container Apps, managed PostgreSQL, private Redis, Blob Storage, Key Vault and CDN. OCI images and provider interfaces keep the application portable; provider procurement, region and capacity remain owner decisions.

Cache and query strategy

  • Public content cache key: verified site/domain + published revision + locale + template/block version. Invalidate after the publish transaction and retain a bounded stale-on-error policy only for approved public content.
  • Property cache key: tenant/site + feed + filter hash + provider mapping + policy version. TTL cannot exceed provider rights or source freshness. Recheck listing availability and attribution before returning cached/indexed IDs. Rights revocation cannot wait for ordinary TTL expiry.
  • Workspace server/client caches include active tenant and permission scope. Organization switching clears previous sensitive query data immediately and cancels in-flight requests. A scope change increments authorization cache generation.
  • Use cursor indexes for CRM and listings; reject pathological wildcards, unsupported filters, unbounded geographic extents and excessive query costs. Begin with PostgreSQL plans on synthetic scale datasets; external search is an explicit later ADR.

sections.title: 4. Module specifications and acceptance criteria
sections.html:
These numbered requirements are the implementation contract. Each module identifies the shared services it needs, owned entities, API operations, UI and testable outcomes. Cross-module commands and event payloads use the shared contracts; module names do not imply separate microservices.

MOD-A · SaaS administration, identity and billing

M1–M2 · Owner: W01 + W03

One organization, identity and entitlement model for agents, offices and product assets. Staff administration uses a separate control-plane context.

Functional requirements

  1. MOD-A-001 Provision an organization through a durable job: seed built-in roles, six configurable pipeline stages, default lead source and business profile; expose pending/ready/failed state. Invitations use a hashed, expiring, one-use token and require the signed-in verified email to match the invitation.
  2. MOD-A-002 Support owner, organization manager, agent, marketing editor, billing administrator and read-only analyst role presets. Permission codes come from the API catalog; scope is own/team/organization. Custom roles cannot grant rights the caller cannot delegate. Lock the organization row during owner changes and reject removal or demotion of its final active owner.
  3. MOD-A-003 Offer organization, office, member and business-profile management with optimistic versions, audit events and visible entitlement limits. An identity may belong to multiple organizations; the active organization selector changes all data, cache and job contexts together.
  4. MOD-A-004 Show account subscription, enabled/pending/disabled capabilities, invoices, annual invoice total and monthly equivalent separately. Preview plan changes, cancellation/resumption, proration, currency, taxes and effective date; require an unexpired preview and explicit acceptance before a financial operation.
  5. MOD-A-005 Stripe webhook reconciliation determines billing state; application entitlements remain explicit records. Duplicate or out-of-order events trigger a current provider-state read, not timestamp-only entitlement changes. Failed provisioning never becomes ready merely because payment succeeded.
  6. MOD-A-006 Super administrators see organization health, provisioning jobs, feature configuration, subscription reconciliation, redacted audit logs and operational summaries. Access to customer records requires a time-bound, reasoned grant and visible staff-session banner; it is not an ordinary tenant role.

MOD-B · Agent workspace, activity and appointments

M2 · Owner: W02 + W03

A daily work surface that reports actual lead, task and integration state rather than unverified productivity narratives.

Functional requirements

  1. MOD-B-001 Render assigned lead activity, overdue/today/upcoming tasks, appointments, pipeline summary, notifications and website/campaign health. Default scope is the current agent; permitted team/organization views are explicit selectors.
  2. MOD-B-002 Every KPI includes definition/version, period, timezone, numerator/denominator where relevant, source and refresh time. Loading, empty, unavailable and ineligible states remain distinct; zero is a valid measured value.
  3. MOD-B-003 Actions open an existing lead/task in a drawer with a shareable route. Quick actions use the same authorization and validation as full pages. Preferences affect layout only, not data-access scope.
  4. MOD-B-004 Appointments reflect verified scheduling/cancellation events. The platform initially integrates a scheduling provider; it does not infer that a booking iframe synchronizes with CRM. Display organization and user timezone labels when they differ.

MOD-D · CRM, leads, deals, tasks and routing

M2 · Owner: W04

Own the commercial relationship model independently of IDX or a white-label CRM provider.

Functional requirements

  1. MOD-D-001 Separate contact identity/channels from a lead opportunity and a deal. Maintain normalized email/phone values, source attribution, optional user-provided intent/timeline, tags, stage history, notes and a communication/activity timeline. Unknown values remain unknown.
  2. MOD-D-002 Provide saved list filters, server pagination, column preferences, bulk selection scope, lead detail drawers and a pipeline view. Default stages are Uncontacted, Attempted Contact, Nurturing, Dead, Under Contract and Closed; organizations can configure their own immutable stage IDs.
  3. MOD-D-003 Routing precedence defaults to first-touch owner, listing-attributed agent, geography, then weighted round robin. Evaluate only active eligible members; serialize distribution state, record the winning rule and fall back to an unassigned queue when no recipient is eligible. Office and tenant boundaries apply to every rule.
  4. MOD-D-004 Score documented engagement signals using a versioned deterministic formula before introducing AI. Show reason codes and last event time; score is sales follow-up prioritization, never housing eligibility, protected-attribute inference or mortgage approval.
  5. MOD-D-005 CSV imports require a scoped signed upload, mapping, preview, row errors, duplicate candidates and an explicit reviewed merge/skip policy. Commit the accepted snapshot with an idempotency key; do not merge automatically across organizations or solely because a household shares a phone.
  6. MOD-D-006 Exports run as jobs with source-scope authorization at request and download, short-lived artifact access, spreadsheet-formula neutralization and audit. Archiving a contact/lead cancels eligible pending sends and marks public organizer relationships according to the retention plan.
  7. MOD-D-007 Tasks require assignee, title, due instant and IANA timezone. Stage, owner and note changes use If-Match or expected version, preserve historical events and return conflict instead of silently overwriting another agent.

  2. MOD-D-AC-2 A listing agent in another organization cannot become owner. Disabled members and round-robin race conditions are handled without lost or cross-office assignments.
  3. MOD-D-AC-3 A stale lead/task update returns 412; the existing event history remains intact. Archived leads do not receive new marketing enrollments.

MOD-C · Real estate website builder, content, domains and forms

M3 · Owner: W05 + W02

Deliver a unified premium builder with independently owned templates and a versioned property-aware block schema.

Functional requirements

  1. MOD-C-001 Use Puck as an editor component behind an adapter; retain platform-owned block documents, schemas and renderer. Ship independently designed agent, brokerage and landing template families. Template definitions are versioned repository assets; tenant customizations become content revisions.
  2. MOD-C-002 Allow page, blog, landing, community, agent and testimonial documents with navigation, slug, SEO title/description, canonical path, social image and noindex settings. Offer hero, text, image, CTA, agent, testimonials, community, listing grid, search, form, map and footer blocks.
  3. MOD-C-003 Save drafts as immutable revisions with optimistic document versions. Publish validates every block, image right, link, form and MLS capability, then atomically updates the revision pointer and emits cache invalidation. Preview and production have distinct hostnames and signed preview access; rollback republishes an existing compatible revision.
  4. MOD-C-004 Unknown/older blocks preserve their data and render a safe editor warning; they cannot be silently dropped or published until migrated. Arbitrary scripts, SQL, unsafe HTML, remote fetch URLs and free-form executable custom CSS are excluded from the initial block contract.
  5. MOD-C-005 Custom domains require ownership verification, a globally unique normalized hostname, TLS provisioning and exact host→site→organization mapping. A verification job never grants a hostname based on an unverified client claim. Detach revokes routing and certificates before the domain can be reassigned.
  6. MOD-C-006 Media uploads are signed, tenant-prefixed, capped and MIME-sniffed, scanned before publication, transformed into responsive derivatives and attached to a rights attestation. Originals remain private unless explicitly permitted; SVG uploads are rejected or sanitized by a vetted pipeline, not embedded as executable user HTML.
  7. MOD-C-007 Versioned form schemas define labels, required fields, bounds, select choices, honeypot/challenge, purpose-specific consent and confirmation. Server validation uses the published version. A durable transaction stores the entry, lead decision and outbox event before acknowledging. Ordinary form entry permits paste and accessible validation.
  8. MOD-C-008 Initial forms do not offer public file uploads or pricing/payment fields. The API upload grant is staff-authenticated; public visitor file uploads require a later quota, scanning and abuse review. These are deferred from the reference Gravity Forms library rather than accidentally promised.
  9. MOD-C-009 Public rendering is server-produced and SEO-friendly. Property blocks use approved public listing projections; a provider supporting only embeds cannot be presented as native searchable feed data. Hidden/deleted/expired listings invalidate page, map, image and alert caches.

M4 · Owner: W06

Listing changes generate deduplicated alert matches; before notification, recheck feed permission, listing availability, alert preference and consent. Inquiry capture routes through the native CRM with source and listing provenance.
  5. Deleted/withdrawn data disappears promptly through listing state, caches, search indexes and scheduled alerts. Missing deletion support requires contract-approved reconciliation.

  7. MOD-F-007 The project owner selected CoreLogic Trestle (now Cotality Trestle) as the provider on 10 October 2026. Target its documented RESO WebAPI adapter; approved Las Vegas connection details and credentials arrive at M6. Confirm the actual board, feed product, participant permissions, endpoint, accessible metadata and display/retention/media rights then; public documentation does not establish account authorization.

MOD-G · Reporting, attribution and product analytics

M2 basics; M7 advanced · Owner: W08

Make platform outcomes auditable and comparable with published definitions rather than blended undocumented scorecards.

Functional requirements

  1. MOD-G-001 Define website session/page engagement, captured/qualified leads, contact rate, stage conversion, campaign submitted/delivered/bounced/clicked activity, pipeline value and listing engagement. Separate counts, unique entities, cohorts and estimates.
  2. MOD-G-002 Metric definitions are versioned JSON contracts with event source, numerator, denominator, exclusion rules, deduplication, timezone and freshness. Initial aggregates live in PostgreSQL; introduce a warehouse/search service only after measured query/retention limits.
  3. MOD-G-003 Campaign conversion joins eligible events to a documented attribution window and reports unattributed records. Email opens may be affected by privacy proxies; never equate opens with confirmed human reading or business conversion.
  4. MOD-G-004 Reporting filters and exports respect underlying agent/team/organization permissions. Raw form/chat payloads and full contact records do not enter anonymous traffic telemetry. Respect approved analytics consent and collection configuration.
  5. MOD-G-005 Display data source, last refresh and unavailable status. Provider metrics retain their original source/window; publisher coverage is reported separately from actual search visibility or AI assistant answers.
  6. MOD-G-006 Provide period comparisons, funnel and pipeline views, campaign/listing drill-down and account operational health. Initial reports are bounded synchronous queries; heavy exports become scoped durable jobs.
SpecificationDecision

  3. MOD-G-AC-3 Unknown/missing provider statistics display unavailable and cannot be averaged into a synthetic success score.
  4. MOD-G-AC-4 An exported report includes metric version, scope, timezone, source period and last refresh; changing a definition preserves old report provenance.

MOD-H · Assistive AI and competitive intelligence

M7 · Owner: W09

Assist people with drafting and understanding verified facts; AI is never a substitute for permission, licensed data rights or publication approval.

Functional requirements

  1. MOD-H-001 Provide optional page/blog drafts, property descriptions, campaign drafts, lead activity summaries, workflow suggestions and analytics explanations. Each job records purpose, requester, context references, prompt/model configuration version, usage, warnings and expiry.
  2. MOD-H-002 Use a server-side OpenAI Responses API adapter with schema-constrained outputs and a configured model selected through evaluation. Do not hard-code a marketing model name as a permanent default. Handle refusal, incomplete output, timeout and schema-invalid results without applying a partial result.
  3. MOD-H-003 Retrieve only tenant-scoped, permission-filtered facts, with an explicit MLS AI-use flag where listing data is involved. Distinguish source facts from generated prose; citations point to verified fields/documents and cannot be fabricated by accepting model-provided IDs blindly.
  4. MOD-H-004 Acceptance of a draft checks the destination write permission and expected revision, then saves a draft/version through the domain service. It never publishes, sends a campaign, changes consent, modifies a billing plan or acts on a lead merely because an AI job succeeded.
  5. MOD-H-005 Lead qualification assistance summarizes voluntarily supplied intent/timeline and interaction history. It must not infer protected characteristics, decide access to housing/credit, or score financial eligibility. Humans review follow-up recommendations.
  6. MOD-H-006 A conversational public-site assistant is a separate later opt-in capability: public published content and permitted listings only, no CRM/customer retrieval. Begin with read-only FAQ/property answers, citations and handoff; property inquiries use the standard consent-aware form, not a hidden AI side effect.
  7. MOD-H-007 Analytics explanations include actual metric definitions and computed values; the model does not calculate financial/KPI truth from prose. A provider-neutral guard prevents arbitrary URL fetching, unapproved tool use and cross-tenant retrieval induced by listing or user prompt injection.
  8. MOD-H-008 Require per-organization cost/request caps, bounded context/output, redacted telemetry, configurable retention and an approved provider data agreement. store:false reduces response persistence where supported but is not a promise of zero provider retention.

  3. MOD-I-003 Report publisher sync coverage, reviews/reputation and source-specific visibility metrics with definitions. Any real query-based AI visibility tracking is a separate explicit measurement feature, not renamed directory coverage.
  4. MOD-I-004 Google Business connection, social scheduling and review-response workflows remain capability/permission gated. AI-assisted review responses are drafts that require human approval and a provider-supported publication method.
  5. MOD-I-005 Reusable brand kits and email/page templates are launch features. Standalone print fulfillment, design packs, mortgage-specific products and advanced creative editors are deferred until product demand, licensing and fulfillment behavior are verified.

MOD-J · Support, integration operations and account health

M2 basics; ongoing · Owner: W03 + W10 + W11

Make provisioning and provider problems visible, recoverable and supportable without invisible staff access.

Functional requirements

  2. MOD-J-002 Expose customer-safe integration status and jobs: queued/running/succeeded/failed/unknown, attempts, last success, safe error code and recommended action. Never display secrets, provider raw payloads or another organization’s support record.
  3. MOD-J-003 Provide staff dashboards for failed provisioning, billing/feed reconciliation, sender eligibility, expired domains and worker lag. Replay is an explicit audited domain action with idempotency and scope validation, not a generic rerun-any-payload button.
  4. MOD-J-004 Document onboarding and contextual help. Replace reference achievement/help clutter with task-relevant learning; do not assume a tutorial link means the named service is integrated.

MOD-K · Full web application and installable iPhone/Android experience

M1 foundation; M2–M7 workflow parity; M8 device gate · Owner: W12 + W02 + W11

Deliver the same complete web application through browsers and home-screen installation on iPhone and Android, without App Store or Google Play distribution.

Functional requirements

  1. MOD-K-001 Implement an HTTPS Progressive Web App using Next.js manifest support, an original icon set, display:standalone, stable manifest id, start URL, app scope and service worker. The workspace remains usable in ordinary browsers without installation. No native wrapper or app-store submission is part of the architecture.
  2. MOD-K-002 Provide platform-appropriate installation guidance: iPhone browser share/menu Add to Home Screen and Android Install/Add to Home Screen. Detect install capability and standalone mode; never show a nonfunctional universal install button or block use behind installation.
  3. MOD-K-003 Make every entitled workflow usable at 360px and larger: CRM capture/edit/tasks, dashboards, builder draft/preview/publish, campaign edit/preview/confirm, property search/inquiry/organizer, reports, settings and authorized administration. Complex canvases have accessible list/form alternatives; do not require a desktop to complete core commands.
  4. MOD-K-004 Respect device safe areas, dynamic viewport height, orientation, virtual keyboards, touch targets, screen readers and system text enlargement. Preserve deep links and navigation history; reauthenticate safely after suspension, external OIDC and hosted billing flows.
  5. MOD-K-005 Cache only approved static application assets and a generic offline screen. Initial release is online-first: no private CRM, session tokens, personalized HTML/RSC, messages, exports, AI results or MLS data in service-worker caches or IndexedDB. Offline mutations are visibly disabled and never reported as saved.
  6. MOD-K-006 Preserve unsaved changes in current tab memory during brief connection loss and warn before navigation/update; process eviction may discard them. After reconnection refetch versions and permissions. Durable offline editing/synchronization is deferred to a separately reviewed data-conflict/security design.
  7. MOD-K-007 Use versioned static asset caches and a waiting-worker update notice. Never force reload while a draft is dirty or a payment/publish/send confirmation is in flight. Reload only after user acceptance or a safe idle transition, and remove obsolete non-sensitive caches.
  8. MOD-K-008 Offer opt-in standards-based Web Push for assigned-lead, task-due and job-failure notices where supported; the in-app inbox remains authoritative. Check capabilities and user gesture, handle denied permission, and keep lock-screen text generic with no contact/property details.
  9. MOD-K-009 Store encrypted, tenant/member-scoped push subscriptions and revoke devices on explicit removal/logout and membership revocation. Validate HTTPS push endpoints against approved provider egress policy; reject local/private hosts. VAPID private keys are server secrets; push clicks open allowlisted same-origin deep links and recheck authorization.
  10. MOD-K-010 M8 requires physical iPhone Safari/browser and installed-home-screen tests, plus Android Chrome/browser and installed tests. Cover sign-in, organization switching, all core workflows, interruptions/offline, SW upgrades, denied push, device removal, keyboard/safe-area behavior and no sensitive persistent caching.

sections.title: 5. Identity, tenancy, permissions and staff administration
sections.html:
OIDC flow: BFF generates state, nonce and PKCE challenge; callback verifies issuer, audience, signature, state, nonce and token lifetime. Link identities by verified issuer + subject, not an email string alone. Store an opaque rotating session server-side and set a Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite cookie. Require fresh authentication for billing, staff grants and high-impact role changes. Preserve browser password managers and paste.

Every organization API checks active membership, current tenant status, permission code, entitlement and row scope. RLS enforces tenant separation; own/team/organization is an additional query policy, never a post-filter applied after returning counts. Teams initially mean offices with explicit active office membership. A read-only aggregate cannot disclose records that individual reads forbid.

PresetAllowed scope / responsibilitiesRestrictions
OwnerOrganization configuration, members, roles, content, CRM, marketing, reports, billing and integrations.Must preserve final active owner; no platform staff permissions. Sensitive export/send/publish actions remain explicit permissions and audit events.
Organization managerOrganization CRM, office/team membership, pipeline/routing, tasks and reports.No billing, staff grant or owner-role delegation by default. Publishing/sending can be assigned explicitly.
AgentOwn contacts/leads/deals/tasks; own dashboard/notifications; approved site/property read access.No organization-wide CRM export, member/routing configuration or sending to another owner’s contacts. Team scope requires an approved office role.
Marketing editorOrganization content/message draft editing, media and campaign design.Publish/send are separate grants; no financial or unrestricted CRM write permissions. Audience preview is constrained by approved recipient scope.
Billing administratorBilling read/manage and invoice access.No default CRM/contact/content permissions.
Read-only analystApproved own/team/organization reporting and relevant read projections.No edits, sends, publishes, data exports or raw contact/message access unless separately granted.
Platform staffControl-plane organization health and operational statistics.Tenant access requires approved time-bound purpose/permission grant. Grant creator cannot self-approve unrestricted customer access; step-up and separate approval policy required.
VisitorOwn saved searches/favorites under a verified published site.No organization APIs or cross-site organizer records. Passwordless login challenges are hashed, short-lived, one-use and rate-limited; identical response prevents email enumeration.

Release feature flags live in reviewed deployment configuration; staff can read active configuration and health, while plan metadata changes use explicit audited platform endpoints. The complete permission-code list is permission-catalog.json and role-presets.json. A code is an operation capability, not sufficient row authorization. The companion built-in role preset file defines explicit code/scope grants; M1 implements and tests them as fixtures. Custom role delegation is the intersection of delegatable codes and the caller’s scope; owner and platform escalation are dedicated guarded commands.

The server opens a transaction and applies transaction-local app.tenant_id, app.actor_id and verified issuer/subject through parameterized set_config calls. Never set persistent pool session context. After commit/rollback the next borrower must see no previous context. Missing context denies rows. Identity bootstrap needs the verified issuer/subject path before the local actor exists; organization provisioning uses a separately reviewed control-plane role, not the ordinary runtime role.

FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY does not constrain superusers or BYPASSRLS roles. Runtime and worker identities must therefore be non-owner, NOSUPERUSER and NOBYPASSRLS; the migration identity is separate. The supplied SQL revokes PUBLIC and defines policies, but intentionally leaves reviewed role/grant provisioning to M1. Use column/table privileges for immutable audit, consent and history evidence; administrative deletion/retention uses a restricted audited worker. PostgreSQL row security

Public requests resolve an exact approved domain to a published site and tenant; a site ID alone is not enough. Reject unknown hosts and untrusted forwarded headers. The public runtime receives only approved read projections plus narrowly scoped form/inquiry commands; it cannot query unrestricted CRM tables. Custom-domain visitor sessions are site-bound and separate from workspace cookies. CSRF/Origin checks apply to cookie-authenticated visitor mutations as well as workspace mutations. Anonymous form anti-abuse uses rate limits, honeypot and optional accessible challenge with server validation.

sections.title: 6. Data model, relationships, indexing and migrations
sections.html:
Canonical schema: schema.sql; structured metadata: data-dictionary.json. There are 72 proposed tables. Business tables use (tenant_id, id) composite primary keys and tenant-scoped foreign keys, preserving isolation even when a caller guesses a valid ID from another organization. Global records are organization, user identity, platform staff and public plan catalog; their access policies differ explicitly.

Model ruleRequired implementation behavior
Identity / membershipuser_identity is globally issuer/subject unique; membership binds identity, organization, role, status and offices. Avoid merging identities by unverified email.
Contact / lead / dealContact owns channels; a lead tracks intent/source/stage/assignment and a deal tracks commercial progress. Contact archival cascades domain cancellation through commands/events, not a blind destructive SQL cascade.
Published revision pointercontent_document.published_revision_id references a revision of the SAME document using a composite FK. Content edits append immutable revisions; publishing/rollback atomically swaps the pointer after version checks.
Campaign versionsAn enrollment references a published campaign version; editing a draft does not rewrite current scheduled actions. Freeze each message snapshot (rendered template, design version/hash and merge-field schema) at campaign publication and copy it into scheduled actions. Workers use this snapshot rather than a mutable message_design row; generation and step references bind actions to cancellation/version checks.
Listing identity(tenant_id, feed_id, source_listing_key) is stable/unique. Public listing ID is platform-owned; source IDs can collide across feeds. Preserve source status and mapping version; unknown status is non-displayed unless explicitly approved.
Domain ownershipNormalized lower-case hostname has global uniqueness. Domain takeover/reassignment needs verified ownership, detach/release audit and CDN/TLS reconciliation; tenant uniqueness alone is insufficient.
Audit / events / jobsEvents and jobs retain references, state, correlation, attempts and safe error codes. Immutability is enforced by grants and approved service methods, not merely by describing a table as an audit log.
JSONBUse for versioned block data, safe configuration, attribution and policy structures validated against schemas. Do not use unrestricted JSONB as an excuse to accept arbitrary fields or secret payloads.
Versions / timestampsEvery business mutation increments row_version and updated_at in the service transaction. The baseline has defaults, not automatic update triggers. Use UTC instants and IANA timezone IDs; monetary currency/amount semantics are explicit per API field.

Indexes and query safeguards

  • Tenant-first B-tree indexes support foreign keys and cursor pagination. CRM uses created_at/id and owner/stage partial indexes for active leads; task due indexes target open assigned tasks. Contact channels use normalized kind/value lookup without implying cross-tenant deduplication.
  • Property search uses tenant/feed/status/price indexes, PostGIS GIST geography and a GIN public-remarks text expression. Combine tenant and policy predicates in every plan; a spatial index alone is not a tenant security mechanism. Radius queries use meters; limit bbox area/results and validate longitude/latitude ordering.
  • Queue dispatch indexes cover pending due actions and unpublished outbox rows. A scheduler enumerates approved organizations through the control plane, then enters each tenant context; the index does not authorize a cross-tenant bypass scan.
  • Measure plans and index write overhead before adding broad JSON indexes. Reporting builds tenant/day aggregates; high-volume activity may be time-partitioned after measured growth. Do not partition all 72 tables in the first migration.

Migration sequence

M1 splits the baseline into reviewed migrations: extensions/schema and functions → global tables → tenant tables/constraints → indexes → policies → runtime/control-plane roles and grants → deterministic role/pipeline fixtures. Test an empty database, a prior-version database, upgrade rollback at the application level and pool reuse under actual roles. CI owns a migration registry and rejects duplicate identifiers.

Use expand → compatible application → batched tenant-aware backfill → validation → contract. Online index creation is a separate nontransactional migration where necessary. Keep the last application release compatible while jobs drain. Roll back application code against compatible schema; destructive rollback is not the default recovery plan. Long backfills checkpoint per tenant and throttle against production load.

Retention proposal — policy decisions, not legal conclusions

Record classInitial design defaultGate / deletion behavior
CRM / deals / notesWhile active subscription and owner-approved business retention apply; no universal automatic duration.M2 establishes owner/jurisdiction policy. Deletion anonymizes eligible contact channels/notes while preserving required minimal evidence. Legal holds override ordinary schedules.
Raw public analytics30 days raw safe event metadata; 13 months nonidentifying aggregates.M7 approves cookies/consent, region and identifiers. Do not store full URLs containing contact data or raw form bodies.

sections.title: 7. API conventions, validation and operation contracts
sections.html:
Normative machine-readable baseline: OpenAPI 3.1.1 contract. The reserved .example host is not a deployed endpoint. All operations declare schemas, security, permission metadata, tenant context, rate policy and standard error responses. The artifact is structurally checked; framework generation and full request conformance require implementation tests. OpenAPI 3.1.1

ConventionContract
Version / transportHTTPS JSON under /v1. Additive optional fields within v1; breaking field meaning, required input or authorization behavior needs reviewed version/deprecation plan. Public site APIs and staff APIs remain separate namespaces.
Schema validationReject unknown command properties, oversized strings/arrays, malformed UUIDs/dates and invalid enum values. Validate dynamic block/provider config against its versioned allowlist. Normalize phone/email cautiously; never convert missing consent to permission.
Business validationCheck priceMin ≤ priceMax, valid bbox [west,south,east,north], geographic extent, supported filters and IANA timezone. Referenced owner/contact/site/lead/campaign/feed IDs must belong to the verified tenant and be in allowed scope.
PaginationOpaque signed cursor; stable sort plus ID tie-breaker, default 25, maximum 100. Cursor binds tenant, actor scope, filter/sort hash and expiry. Changed filters invalidate the cursor. Do not expose raw SQL offsets for large feeds.
FilteringCRM page filter is the LeadFilter contract; endpoints reject fields that lack semantics for that resource. Listing filter is JSON-encoded ListingCriteria; unsupported capabilities return 422 with field details rather than being ignored.
Mutations / concurrencyIdempotency-Key on state-changing commands. PATCH/PUT require If-Match; publish commands include expected document/version IDs. Return 412 for stale versions; preserve editor work for manual conflict resolution.
IdempotencyStore tenant + actor + route + key + canonical request hash and outcome. Same key/same hash replays outcome; same key/different hash returns 409. Retain key records at least 24 hours and longer for durable provider side effects until reconciliation is complete. Provider dedupe windows are separately discovered.
Session / CSRFVerified BFF cookie, current active membership and row policy; X-CSRF-Token plus exact Origin for workspace writes. Site-bound visitor cookie writes require equivalent CSRF protection. Public webhook authentication is provider signature verification, never a workspace cookie.
Asynchronous commands202 returns durable job reference and state; polling getJob returns pending/running/succeeded/failed with safe error/retry information. Enforce job ownership/module scope. A successful enqueue is not evidence of a successful provider operation.
Errorsapplication/problem+json follows RFC 9457 with type/title/status/code/detail/traceId and safe validation fields. No SQL, raw provider errors, secret URLs or other tenant existence details. RFC 9457
Planning rate defaults300 read and 120 write requests/member/minute; AI 20 jobs/member/hour plus organization cost cap; public forms 10/IP/site/10 minutes. These are configurable product defaults, not vendor quota claims. Also limit body sizes, global concurrency and tenant storage/send volume.
Quota feedback429 includes Retry-After and trace ID; scoped counters do not reveal other tenants’ quotas. Third-party rate failures use bounded delayed jobs and visible degraded state.
WebhooksRoute provider/connection identifies an existing approved connection; exact provider payload is verified before internal normalization. Transactionally store inbox event and deduplication record before 200 acknowledgment. Reject invalid/replayed signatures and never trust payload tenant IDs.

Stripe uses Stripe-Signature, Twilio uses X-Twilio-Signature, and Resend uses the Svix header set. The route selects only that provider’s verifier. Capture raw bytes before JSON parsing where required; use configured canonical public URLs for signatures, timestamp tolerances, secret rotation and provider event-ID deduplication. A valid signature from another provider never authorizes this route. Stripe webhook verification Resend webhooks

Command example: capture, route and return a durable receipt

{
  "method": "POST",
  "path": "/v1/public/sites/{siteId}/form-submissions",
  "headers": {
    "Idempotency-Key": "fixture-submission-0001"
  },
  "body": {
    "formId": "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001",
    "formVersion": 1,
    "values": {
      "name": "Sample Contact",
      "email": "sample@example.invalid",
      "email_marketing": false,
      "sms_marketing": false
    }
  },
  "note": "Values must match the published form schema, including explicit consent fields. Attribution comes from validated server-side site/session context. No real contact or consent claim."
}
