sections.title: 8. Events, durable jobs and orchestration
sections.html:
Commit the domain mutation and outbox event together. The dispatcher publishes the same eventId until acknowledged; consumers maintain a tenant/event/consumer dedupe ledger in the durable job/inbox records. Use at-least-once transport and idempotent effects, without claiming universal exactly-once message delivery. Correlation IDs link the browser command, transaction, job and provider reference.

The event-envelope schema defines tenant, event ID/type/version, aggregate, occurrence/ingestion times, causation and a small reference-only payload. Each listed type uses the same payload shape: resourceId is the aggregate record; resourceVersion is its committed version; relatedResourceIds are scoped references, not customer data. Consumers reload data under current authorization before acting.

Event typeProducer / aggregateConsumers / effect
lead.capturedCRM / leadRouting, dashboard and marketing trigger evaluation.
lead.assignedCRM / leadOwner notification and scoped metrics.
lead.stage_changedCRM / leadVersioned automation eligibility and pipeline aggregates.
contact.archivedCRM / contactCancel future enrollments; suppress eligible alerts and remove ordinary contact views.
task.dueScheduler / taskScoped notifications; never arbitrary customer messages.
site.publishedCMS / documentCDN invalidation, sitemap and publishing audit.
form.submittedCMS / form_entryCRM capture reconciliation and safe source metrics; no raw values on event bus.
campaign.enrolledMarketing / enrollmentCreate generation-bound scheduled actions.
campaign.cancelledMarketing / enrollmentInvalidate unsent actions, preserve receipts.
delivery.receiptDelivery adapter / delivery_attemptUpdate terminal state, suppression/consent via explicit approved commands and aggregates.
consent.changedMarketing / consent_eventInvalidate sending eligibility and cancel/suppress affected pending actions.
listing.changedProperty / listingSearch/cache update and licensed alert matching.
listing.withdrawnProperty / listingInvalidate every public/cache/media/alert surface.
subscription.reconciledBilling / subscriptionUpdate explicit entitlement projection and provisioning state.
integration.state_changedIntegrations / integration_connectionConnector readiness notifications and safe job scheduling.
ai.draft_readyAI / ai_jobNotify requester; no automatic content/action mutation.

Leases use a bounded lease_until and heartbeat, with conditional state/version updates. Claim one due action via transaction and row locking; release the database transaction before external calls. Persist an attempt and stable provider idempotency key before sending. A timeout after provider acceptance becomes unknown/reconciling; retry only after receipt/provider query or an explicitly approved manual decision. Provider keys may have finite windows, so local attempt history outlives them. Resend delivery idempotency

Email unsubscribe links use signed purpose/channel tokens without requiring login; the dedicated one-click endpoint accepts the mail client POST form with token in the URL, no cookies/CSRF/session and no redirect. GET link previews never withdraw consent. Configure List-Unsubscribe/List-Unsubscribe-Post and provider DKIM coverage per RFC 8058; redact token query strings from access logs. Cancellation increments the enrollment generation and cancels future pending actions. A worker rechecks generation immediately before dispatch; cancellation cannot retract a message already accepted by a provider. Quiet hours and send dates use recipient timezone if known, otherwise approved organization default. For daylight saving gaps use the first valid instant after the gap, and for repeated times the first occurrence; expose computed send time in previews. Birthday on 29 February defaults to 28 February in non-leap years only after owner approval; do not silently invent greeting policy. RFC 8058 one-click unsubscribe

FailureRecovery and user state
Redis unavailableCommitted jobs remain in PostgreSQL. Recover due wakeups; show delayed pending status.
Worker crash before provider callExpired lease resumes with same action/attempt identity after revalidation.
Worker crash after provider acceptanceReconcile receipt/provider reference; do not blindly resend.
Outbox duplicate / consumer crashSame event ID and consumer dedupe ledger prevent duplicate domain effects.
Provider 429 / 5xxRespect Retry-After; bounded exponential backoff with jitter, circuit breaker and organization concurrency limit.
Permanent validation / rights / consent failureTerminal safe error with actionable reason; no automated retry until state/input changes.
Database commit failureNo durable command outcome; retry with original idempotency key. Never return succeeded.
Poison jobBounded attempts then quarantine/dead-letter with redacted context; operator replay is audited and revalidates current authorization.

sections.title: 9. Las Vegas MLS and Trestle integration architecture
sections.html:
Owner-selected provider: CoreLogic Trestle / Cotality Trestle. The owner supplied this choice during drafting. Public documentation confirms a RESO WebAPI path; no Las Vegas account, feed entitlement, participant approval or credentials have been verified. M1 freezes interfaces, M5 uses synthetic fixtures, and M6 connects the authorized Trestle feed.

Trestle’s current documentation identifies a Cotality API base, OAuth client-credentials authentication and OData metadata discovery. Configure token/data origins from the approved connection rather than hard-code legacy hostnames shown in older examples. Read the returned token expiry, cache server-side, refresh before expiration with a single-flight lock and keep secrets in Key Vault references. Do not assume refresh-token support. Trestle WebAPI getting started

Target a Trestle RESO WebAPI adapter as the first live implementation, preferably licensed replication for native search when approved. Trestle documents real-time queries and replication; this does not prove the owner’s feed permits every resource, field, display status or use. Do not use its sample feed: the user’s development constraint remains our own fictional data. Trestle capabilities FAQ

Transport modeData pathProduct implications
Replication — preferred if licensedAuthorized Trestle change pages → normalize → tenant/feed-scoped PostgreSQL → search.Native list/map/detail/organizer/alerts only within approved field, media, cache and notification rights.
Live queryAPI → provider adapter with bounded filters → normalize approved response.No assumed full local inventory. Short cache only if licensed; saved searches store criteria, not unrestricted listing snapshots. Alerts require an approved polling/provider mechanism.
Embed — alternative provider capabilityPublic site loads an approved provider origin and documented integration surface.Native search/map/organizer may be unavailable or provider-owned. Approved inquiry integration may route to CRM; no assumed postMessage events, scraping or listing ingestion. Trestle embed support is not claimed.

The type-only MLS adapter contract discriminates these modes, capabilities, normalized listing identity, secret access and display policy. It is a specification, not an implemented connection. Future regional providers implement the same ports; do not share feed rows across organizations unless both licensing and access policies explicitly permit it. RESO defines standards rather than granting data access. RESO Web API

Trestle-specific synchronization plan

Use ModificationTimestamp for property changes and PhotosChangeTimestamp for media refresh planning. Trestle explains that incremental updates alone do not discover records that disappear; implement complete authorized key reconciliation. A partial/failed key scan must never be interpreted as deletion. Use a scan generation, commit the complete seen-key set, and only then withdraw absent keys. Bound mass-update concurrency and make progress visible. Trestle scaling and reconciliation

Follow @odata.nextLink as an opaque approved-origin continuation. Use Trestle’s documented replication extension when appropriate rather than synthesize arbitrary skip offsets. Compile filters from a typed allowlist and encode values; never accept raw client OData expressions. Confirm OData resource/enum metadata for the approved feed and preserve source names where normalization differs. Trestle query reference

ConcernImplementation rule
Feed identity / credentialsmls_feed stores provider=trestle, approved connection reference, mode, policy/mapping version and health; secrets live outside ordinary tables. A worker resolves credentials from its verified tenant/feed context, not from a user-supplied URL.
Initial loadPersist a run and request boundary; fetch a bounded page, schema-validate and normalize, transactionally upsert by source key and emit changed/withdrawn references. Advance the page checkpoint only after that page’s commit. Idempotent replay is mandatory.
Incremental watermarkUse source timestamps, deterministic key tie-breakers when supported and configurable overlap; do not use the worker clock as the last-source-update watermark. Track latest fully processed boundary, not the largest timestamp seen before failure.
Pagination securityValidate every returned next-link origin/path against the connection allowlist before attaching tokens. Reject redirects to unknown/private hosts. Expired continuation restarts a bounded overlapping run with idempotent upserts.
Status / deletionMap StandardStatus plus source-specific restrictions. Active/pending/closed visibility depends on licensed policy; unknown statuses fail closed. Reconciliation handles missing/deleted/Internet-withheld records and invalidates search, map, details, media, SEO, featured blocks and alert work.
MediaUse provider URLs, approved signed proxy or licensed copied images according to contract. Store source media key/order/change timestamp and expiry. Scan permitted downloads, use bounded transforms and remove derived copies on withdrawal/termination. Never treat a publicly reachable MediaURL as permission to retain it.
Search / mapsPostGIS/text filtering and normalized criteria are shared by list and map. Enforce result/extent limits. Suppressed address also suppresses exact coordinates, structured data, accessible image text and SEO metadata unless policy explicitly permits a different projection.
AlertsUnique match key includes tenant/feed/listing/source change/search/preference generation. Recheck latest listing and feed rights plus current visitor preference/consent at delivery. A detail link that later withdraws shows unavailable, not a stale snapshot.
Inquiry / attributionResolve listing server-side under current display policy, capture feed/listing/source identifiers, campaign/source context and published form version, then create one CRM contact/lead activity through the shared capture command. Never trust caller-provided brokerage or assigned agent IDs.
Quota / retryDiscover the connection’s API and media budgets from approved docs/response headers; configure token buckets per connection and separate media work. Do not treat public example quotas as this account’s quota. Respect 429/Retry-After; bounded backoff/circuit breaker and safe health states.
Auth failureOne synchronized token renewal after a genuine expiry; repeated 401 disables the connection and alerts an operator. Do not endlessly retry revoked/invalid credentials or log Authorization.
FreshnessApproved refresh interval, allowed maximum age, source delay and retention are separate fields. Unknown max age blocks live activation. Data past allowed age is unavailable; a generic stale label cannot authorize prohibited display.
Partner display policyVersioned rights matrix includes required attribution/logo/disclaimer/links, statuses, fields, address/coordinates, media/cache/alerts/AI rights, retention and purge rules. Screenshots and source-to-display checks are M6 evidence.
MonitoringPer-feed last successful page/run/reconciliation, source freshness distribution, failed pages, lag, quota resets, mapping rejects and withdrawal propagation. Redacted traces include source key references where permitted; no private source payload dump.
Termination / revocationDisable serving immediately, cancel unsent alerts, invalidate caches/search and purge storage per approved rules. Keep minimal permitted audit references. Restore drills cannot reenable a revoked feed.

Canonical field mapping baseline

ListingKey + originating/source systemsource_listing_key within approved tenant/feed; retain board/system mapping reference.Do not infer globally unique keys across feeds.
StandardStatus; MlsStatusstatus + source_status + mapping version.Unknown/off-market non-displayed unless approved.

sections.title: 12. Full web application on iPhone and Android — no app stores
sections.html:
Mandatory owner requirement: the complete product is a web application and an installable home-screen app on iPhone and Android. Distribution is HTTPS and browser installation; no Apple App Store or Google Play release, native wrapper or separate native codebase is required.

Use Next.js manifest support and a small reviewed service worker. The workspace origin is the primary installable app; public agent sites remain fully responsive browser experiences and may optionally have their own independent manifests later. A workspace installation does not carry a customer site’s branding or merge cross-origin sessions. Next.js PWA guide

iPhone guidance uses the browser share/menu path to Add to Home Screen; Android uses the browser’s Install/Add to Home Screen capability. Show a platform guide when no programmatic install event exists, and hide prompts after standalone launch. Safari 26 also expands web-app installation behavior, so capability checks and current device testing are preferable to a rigid user-agent-only rule. Browser installation behavior Safari 26 web-app changes

PWA contractImplementation
Manifest / iconsStable id, name/short_name, start_url=/dashboard, scope=/, display=standalone, theme/background colors. Original 192/512 PNG, separate maskable 512 and Apple touch icon; owner-approved brand. Manifest specification example references future icon deliverables, not existing app assets.
Shell / navigationSame authenticated app and module permissions. Safe-area insets, 100dvh with fallback, orientation/keyboard-aware controls, readable forms and touch targets. Do not rely on browser back chrome in standalone mode.
Mobile functional parityEvery entitled core command has a 360px path, including content editing/publishing, message/workflow editing and billing/settings. Use forms/lists where a canvas or third-party editor is unsuitable; mobile is not a read-only companion.
Offline initial scopeStatic shell, local safe assets and generic offline guidance only. No persistent private business data or queued offline writes. In-memory unsaved inputs may survive brief disconnects but not OS process eviction; communicate that limit.
Service-worker network policyAllowlist hashed safe assets. Never cache authentication, API responses, personalized HTML/RSC, CRM, billing, AI, signed downloads or MLS pages/media. Do not apply a catch-all navigation cache. PWA cache/update policy.
Mutation recoveryIf connection drops after a submit, preserve the command idempotency key and query outcome after reauthentication/reconnection. Refetch current versions/scope; unknown is never saved. Initial release disables new offline financial/send/publish/edit commands. Authenticated API and personalized HTML/RSC responses also use Cache-Control: private, no-store; service-worker exclusion alone is insufficient.
UpdatesServe SW/manifest with controlled revalidation; content-hashed static assets. A waiting update shows notice and activates after user acceptance/safe idle, with dirty-draft/in-flight-command guards. Delete only obsolete non-sensitive caches.
Auth / hosted providersTest OIDC callback and Stripe return in browser and standalone contexts; external links may use browser context. Return to a signed allowed deep link, preserve job reference, and reauthenticate when session state is unavailable. No embedded payment/identity assumption.
Push / badgesOpt-in feature-detected Web Push and optional badging. Device record bound to active member/tenant and preference topics; in-app inbox authoritative. Generic lock-screen text such as “You have a new workspace update”, no contact names/addresses.
Push transport securityServer-held VAPID private key; encrypted endpoint/keys; vetted HTTPS egress destinations, no arbitrary URL fetch. Remove invalid/410 devices and revoke on removal/logout/membership revocation. A notification click uses an allowlisted same-origin path and normal authorization.
Background limitsAll business scheduling runs on server workers. Do not depend on iOS/Android keeping a tab or service worker alive, background sync availability, silent push or push delivery guarantees.
Device acceptancePhysical iPhone Safari browser + home-screen app and Android Chrome browser + installed app, current and previous supported OS/browser versions at release. Desktop Chrome/Edge/Safari/Firefox browser compatibility; Playwright emulation supplements physical checks.

WebKit documents home-screen Web Push on supported iOS versions and a permission request triggered by direct user interaction. Installing alone does not grant notification permission. Unsupported or denied push still leaves the complete app and in-app inbox usable. WebKit home-screen push

M1 includes manifest/SW/cache seams; M2 validates CRM and account mobile workflows; each later module passes mobile command parity; M8 verifies physical installs, safe areas, keyboard, authentication, push denial/revocation, offline behavior and update recovery. Public hosting and icons are future implementation work; this TDD does not claim an installable app exists yet.

Request flow: validate ai.use plus all source read permissions → build minimal tenant-scoped context → reject unlicensed listing use → enforce budget → call provider with configured model/prompt version and strict JSON Schema → handle refusal/incomplete output → validate schema, citation IDs and safety constraints → store expiring draft → human acceptance with destination draft permission/version. Database facts and retrieved text are untrusted content, never higher-priority tool instructions.

Structured Outputs improves schema adherence but does not prove factual correctness. Validate claims against approved source facts, handle refusals, and separate evaluation from runtime schema validation. Use Responses text.format with a strict schema or the supported SDK equivalent selected at M7; no credential is required for the blueprint. Structured Outputs limitations

Choose model by quality/cost/latency measurements on the platform’s datasets, then pin deployment configuration and prompt/schema versions. Provider retention and regional processing require an approved data agreement. store:false is not a zero-retention guarantee; verify actual account controls and provider terms before sending sensitive customer data. OpenAI data controls

Proposed release evaluation gateTarget / evidence
Schema and permission enforcement100% of accepted drafts pass server schema and citation-reference validation; zero cross-tenant or out-of-scope disclosures in negative tests.
FactualityNo unsupported critical property/financial claim in the evaluation set; at least 95% supported fact assertions in reviewed sampled drafts. These are project targets, not achieved scores.
Human control100% of acceptance tests save drafts only; zero automatic publish/send/billing/consent actions.
Safety / injectionAdversarial listing/page instructions cannot execute tools or access private facts. Eligibility/protected-trait requests decline inappropriate classification and offer allowed intent summaries.
Useful abstentionMissing facts and source denial produce clear abstention/warnings, never fabricated answers. Include refusal and truncated-output fixtures.
Cost / latencyApproved per-purpose token/output ceiling and tenant monthly budget; record measured p50/p95 and cost before enabling the feature. No price estimate without selected current model/pricing.
Dataset / reviewMinimum initial 200 synthetic/redacted cases distributed across purposes, failure states, tenants and adversarial inputs; version rubric, results and human reviewer disposition.

AI worker cannot use domain write/publish/send credentials. Allowed tools, if introduced later, are read-only scoped ports with schema validation and egress restrictions. Retrieval never follows arbitrary URLs from listing remarks or user instructions. Audit references capture model/prompt/context IDs and review outcome without duplicating unrestricted customer data in telemetry.

sections.title: 17. Operations, scaling, reliability and delivery standards
sections.html:
Capacity assumptions are planning inputs, not observed reference-platform traffic: initial 500 organizations, 5,000 members, 50 API requests/second with short 5× bursts, up to two million contacts and 100,000 allowed listings per regional feed. Validate/replace this envelope with owner forecasts at M1 and measured representative datasets before sizing production. Do not create those listings from real MLS data in development.

Proposed targetMeasurement / operational requirement
Availability99.9% monthly platform availability within approved launch scope; define maintenance/dependency treatment and error-budget action. Provider outages have visible degraded flows.
Workspace APIp95 ≤400ms for ordinary warm reads; public property query p95 ≤800ms at agreed load/filter cases. Separate provider-query latency from platform processing.
Web UXTarget p75 LCP ≤2.5s, INP ≤200ms, CLS ≤0.1 on representative mobile connectivity; measure real-user safe telemetry and synthetic runs. These are goals, not audited performance.
Bundle budgetInitial authenticated compressed JS target ≤350KB; public non-map page ≤200KB. Lazy-load builders, maps/charts and provider widgets. Record actual measured deltas and revise budget through ADR if base framework cost requires it.
JobsDefine per-purpose latency SLO: ordinary capture notifications within 60 seconds; sending and MLS cadence according to approved policies, not a universal guessed refresh interval. Queue lag alarms precede policy breach.
RecoveryProposed RPO ≤15 minutes, RTO ≤4 hours; managed PITR plus verified restore, object lifecycle and queue recovery. M8 must demonstrate with evidence.
Provider budgetsPer-tenant/provider concurrency, request quotas, monthly spend/send/storage caps and circuit breakers. A busy organization cannot starve others.
Search / reporting scaleLoad-test indexed filters and safe aggregates with EXPLAIN plans; introduce a warehouse/external index only after measured need and privacy/rights review.

Development/staging/production use distinct databases, buckets, identities, domains, queues, secret scopes and provider modes. Preview deployments contain only synthetic identities/listings and no-delivery transports; deny network routes to live feed/send endpoints where practical. Startup validates environment schema and refuses a production live feed with mock/synthetic mode or unresolved policy.

CI gates: format/lint → strict types → OpenAPI/event/schema validation and generation drift → unit/UI tests → real PostgreSQL/PostGIS migration/RLS tests → provider mock contracts → relevant E2E and accessibility → image/dependency/secret scan → immutable OCI artifacts with SBOM. Preview checks are reversible; production deployment follows the concrete M8 release decision.

Deploy compatible database expansion first, then API/workers/web, monitor canary tenants and drain/advance jobs safely. Feature flags contain new behavior without bypassing entitlements/rights. Roll back images while schema stays compatible; use explicit restore for data incidents. SW update handling cannot force mobile clients into an incompatible contract without a supported API overlap period.

Runbook / monitorRequired evidence
Tenant/security incidentRevoke sessions/grants/device notices, isolate affected provider, preserve safe audit and investigate scope. Named incident owner and escalation path.
Billing reconciliationCurrent provider subscription read, idempotent projection, failed-provisioning recovery and customer-safe status.
MLS freshness/withdrawalLast run/page/key scan, quota/mapping failures, block stale serving and prove purge propagation.
Communication unknown stateReceipt/query/manual reconciliation decision; do not use generic retry for uncertain sends.
Queue/cache lossRecover committed due jobs/outbox, verify dedupe and quotas; Redis is not the sole schedule.
Database/object restoreRestore isolated copy, run integrity/RLS checks, reapply deletion/rights revocations, compare job generations and perform approved cutover.
PWA release/updateManifest/icon checks, SW static allowlist, waiting-update behavior, deep-link/session return and physical-device results.
ObservabilityStructured redacted logs, trace IDs, error ratios, queue lag, provider errors, DB pool/locks, cache hit/expiry, costs and scoped health. No raw PII in telemetry by default.

Manage keys through workload identity/secret manager, rotate provider credentials and retain audit references only. Use separate database migration/runtime roles, encrypted storage, private connections and least-privilege object prefixes. Infrastructure is versioned Terraform; owner selects region, sizing and contractual controls. Costs remain a capacity worksheet at M1/M4/M6/M7 rather than fabricated totals.

sections.title: 18. Security, privacy and risk controls
sections.html:
Use OWASP ASVS Level 2 as the initial verification scope and track applicable controls. This is an engineering target, not a certification or completed security audit. Build threat tests alongside modules; do not postpone tenant isolation to M8. OWASP ASVS

Threat / riskRequired mitigation and negative test
IDOR / cross-tenant leaksVerified membership + own/team/org policy + composite FK/RLS. Test IDs, counts, search, caches, exports, jobs, media and staff grants with A/B organizations and real pooled connections.
Privilege escalation / owner raceDelegation intersection, locked last-owner invariant, step-up for sensitive grants, no staff permission through tenant roles. Test concurrent demotions and forged office ownership.
Public domain takeoverExact normalized host ownership, global domain uniqueness, verified TXT/TLS lifecycle, trusted proxy config. Test unknown host, stale ownership and forwarded-host spoofing.
XSS / editor contentRegistered schemas, sanitized rich text, safe URLs, restrictive CSP with reviewed provider origins, SVG sanitize/reject. No arbitrary tenant executable JS/HTML injection.
SSRF / media / push / continuationsAllowlisted origins/protocols, vetted egress and redirect policy, reject localhost/private ranges/DNS rebinding. Never attach MLS credentials to an arbitrary nextLink or user URL.
CSV / uploadsBounded parse/file size, content/MIME sniff, scan/quarantine, tenant object prefix, formula-safe export, explicit dedupe preview. Test spreadsheet formulas and malicious file extensions.
Webhook forgery/replayExact provider verifier/raw body/canonical URL, timestamp tolerance, connection binding, dedupe event ID and current-state reconciliation.
Stale consent / duplicate sendsCurrent eligibility at dispatch, stable attempt keys, bounded leases/generations, unknown-state reconciliation and explicit unsubscribe/STOP handling.
MLS license/address leakageFail-closed rights/expiry, sanitization before cache/SEO/map/AI, complete key reconciliation and termination purge. Test metadata, thumbnails and old alert paths.
AI prompt injection / data disclosureScoped minimal facts, no arbitrary fetch/tools, schema/citation checks, model evaluations, human review and separate draft-only acceptance.
Private offline/PWA leaksNo sensitive service-worker/IndexedDB caching, safe generic shell, logout/switch purge and in-memory clearing; test physical device storage after private workflows.
Lock-screen privacyGeneric push content, no contact/listing details, authorized click route and revocation/current membership checks.
Provider dependency / budget riskAdapters/mocks/capabilities, timeout/circuit breaker, spend cap and no misleading success. Procurement is a milestone gate.
Dependency / recovery defectsPinned secure versions, SBOM/scans, migration compatibility, PITR/object/queue restore drill and real device update checks.

Privacy choices are owner/jurisdiction decisions at M2/M4/M7: disclosure/consent language, communication and quiet-hour policy, data-subject handling, cookie/analytics purpose, retention/holds and provider processing agreements. This TDD proposes mechanisms and engineering gates; it does not claim a particular policy satisfies all laws. Do not collect protected attributes for scoring or housing eligibility. Preserve only minimal licensed/necessary data.

Exports use a durable scoped job and short-lived authorized download gateway. Recheck current membership/role before signing, and avoid direct forever-public object URLs. Import commits and contact merges audit review choices. Consent withdrawals append evidence and suppress future sends; deleting a contact does not erase necessary suppression into renewed eligibility.
